title: Understanding the Angular Workspace knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Understanding the Angular Workspace”?
options: Understanding the Angular Workspace helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Understanding the Angular Workspace means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Understanding the Angular Workspace removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Understanding the Angular Workspace should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Understanding the Angular Workspace helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Understanding the Angular Workspace is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Workspace configuration” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Workspace configuration” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Workspace configuration” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Workspace configuration” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Workspace configuration” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Workspace configuration” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Workspace configuration” under Understanding the Angular Workspace. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Understanding the Angular Workspace”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
